key_insight: Trigonal selenium appears intrinsically defect tolerant: even though point defects create deep gap states, both nonradiative and radiative defect-assisted recombination are too weak to explain the observed efficiency losses.
engineering_relevance: This supports t-Se as a promising wide-band-gap absorber for tandem and indoor photovoltaics, where defect robustness can reduce strict materials-control requirements.
method: First-principles calculations of defect-assisted Shockley-Read-Hall recombination
Large, chemically diverse set of point defects in trigonal selenium
Comparison of radiative vs nonradiative capture across defect level, relaxation, charge state, and doping conditions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports large lattice reorganizations and recombination energy releases of at least 0.5 E_G per event, which strongly suppress nonradiative multi-phonon emission and keep calculated defect-assisted losses too small to explain device performance limits.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on idealized first-principles defect models, so real devices may still be affected by defect complexes, interfaces, disorder, or processing-related impurities not included here.
paper_title: Defect Tolerance in Trigonal Selenium Photovoltaics
